meta.triageRationale: One story in one module with a clear approach. The cross-file pass (src/indexer/cross-file-resolver.ts) already dispatches pending rows by kind through PASS2_KINDS ({CALLS, INHERITS, IMPLEMENTS}) into resolveCall / resolveInheritance, promotes single matches with evidence 'inferred' via promoteResolvedBatch, and classes ambiguous / no-candidate rows. The change adds REFERENCES (language sql) to that dispatch with a name matcher over the repository's table/view entities (schema-qualified or bare, unquoted, case-insensitive) and keeps classifyUnattempted from classing those rows 'not-attempted'. No schema or storage change: REFERENCES pending rows, the table/view kinds and the evidence byte already exist (s1/s7/s9). There is one small design choice (how a bare name matches a schema-qualified definition, and the settle-mode scope, which re-attempts only rows from committed files). That stays within a small story, not a feature.

summary.prose: A SQL view or table that names a table or view defined in another .sql file of the repository now gets its REFERENCES edge, written by the cross-file pass with evidence 'inferred'. Before this, the edge stayed pending forever. Names match as SQL compares unquoted names: case-insensitively, a qualified name only its own schema's definition, and a bare name any definition with that last segment. Several candidates stay ambiguous and are never guessed. Saving the file that defines a table also resolves the references that were waiting on it, without waiting for a full index.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Resolve SQL table and view references across files

api.name: PASS2_KINDS

returns.meaning: The pending kinds Pass 2 resolves by name: CALLS, INHERITS, IMPLEMENTS and now REFERENCES.

postconditions: Contains REFERENCES, so classifyUnattempted no longer classes a pending REFERENCES row 'not-attempted'; Pass 2 classes it instead.

api.name: runPass2
api.signature: function runPass2(opts: CrossFileResolveOpts, mode: CrossFileMode, index: EntityIndex): Promise<{ resolved: number; ambiguous: number; stillUnresolved: number }>

parameters.name: opts
parameters.purpose: The repository, db and (settle) committed files.

parameters.name: index
parameters.purpose: The repository's entities, now with the SQL name index.

returns.type: Promise<{ resolved: number; ambiguous: number; stillUnresolved: number }>

preconditions: A REFERENCES row is attempted only when its from-entity's language is 'sql'; any other REFERENCES row is skipped as today.
postconditions: A sql REFERENCES row goes to a new resolveSqlReference(row, index): ResolveIntent, a sibling of resolveCall and resolveInheritance. The per-row dispatch at src/indexer/cross-file-resolver.ts:560-562 becomes three-way: CALLS to resolveCall, REFERENCES to resolveSqlReference, INHERITS/IMPLEMENTS to resolveInheritance. A REFERENCES row whose from-entity is not language 'sql' returns UNRESOLVED without a class change.
Exactly one candidate: the row is promoted through promoteResolvedBatch with evidence 'inferred'.
Several candidates: the row is classed 'ambiguous' with meta.candidates (the ids); no edge is written.
No candidate: the row is classed 'no-candidate' with reason 'no-match'.
The from-entity itself is never a candidate.

In settle mode, after rowsInScope returns the committed files' own rows, runPass2 also takes the repository's pending sql REFERENCES rows whose name could match a table or view that a committed file defines (read with listUnresolvedRelations for the repository, filtered by kind, language and name; each row at most once). When no committed file defines a table or view, settle mode reads exactly what it reads today. rowsInScope itself is unchanged, so its three callers (classifyFileTargets at src/indexer/cross-file-resolver.ts:244, runPass1b at :447 and runPass2 at :524) keep their behaviour.

returns.meaning: Gains sqlByName: Map<string, Entity[]> over sql table/view entities. Each is keyed by its lower-cased full name, and also by its lower-cased last segment when the name is qualified (marked so a bare reference can match it).

dataModelChanges.entity: REFERENCES edge between SQL tables/views across files
dataModelChanges.details: Endpoints and direction: from a table or view entity (language 'sql') to the table or view it names, now also when the target is defined in another file of the same repository. Cardinality: many-to-one per name; one REFERENCES per distinct name per from-entity, as the reader writes it. Ownership: the reader writes it pending, and the cross-file pass promotes it. Evidence: 'inferred' for a cross-file match ('extracted' for a same-file one, unchanged). Compatibility: no new kind, byte or schema version; a pending row that was classed 'no-candidate'/'not-attempted' is re-attempted at the next full, repository or (by name) settle pass. Matching: unquoted names compare case-insensitively. A qualified reference 'app.users' matches only a definition named 'app.users'. A bare reference 'users' matches a definition named 'users', or any qualified definition whose last segment is 'users'.

errorCases.scenario: Two files define a table of the same qualified name (for example two migrations both CREATE TABLE app.users)
errorCases.detection: resolveSqlReference finds more than one sql table/view entity under the reference's lower-cased name
errorCases.response: The row is classed 'ambiguous' with meta.candidates listing both ids; no edge is written
errorCases.userImpact: The reference stays pending, with its candidates visible; nothing wrong is asserted

errorCases.scenario: A reference names a table that no file of the repository defines (an external or system table, such as pg_catalog.pg_class)
errorCases.detection: No entry under the name, and none under the bare last segment
errorCases.response: The row is classed 'no-candidate' with reason 'no-match'
errorCases.userImpact: The reference stays pending, classed so it does not count as awaiting a target

errorCases.scenario: A REFERENCES row whose from-entity is missing from the index (deleted since the row was listed)
errorCases.detection: resolveSqlReference looks the from-entity up as resolveCall does (src/indexer/cross-file-resolver.ts:727-729: byFile, then index.byId; undefined returns UNRESOLVED)
errorCases.response: Left as it is (UNRESOLVED intent with no class change); the next pass sees the deletion

A bare reference 'users' with definitions 'app.users' and 'audit.users'
A bare reference 'users' with definitions 'users' and 'app.users'

edgeCases.input: A qualified reference 'app.users' with a bare definition 'users' only
edgeCases.expected: No candidate: the qualified name says the schema, and the bare definition does not

edgeCases.input: A reference written 'APP.Users' to a definition 'app.users'
edgeCases.expected: Resolved: unquoted names compare case-insensitively (the reader already unquoted the text)

edgeCases.input: A view that references itself by name (recursive view)
edgeCases.expected: The from-entity is never a candidate; the reader already links a same-file reference

edgeCases.input: Settle after saving b.sql, which newly defines orgs; a.sql (not saved) has a pending reference to orgs
edgeCases.expected: The pending row from a.sql is re-attempted in the same settle and resolved

edgeCases.input: A REFERENCES row from a non-sql entity
edgeCases.expected: Not attempted by the SQL matcher; skipped exactly as before

invariantsToPreserve.text: An ambiguous name writes no edge; it stays pending with its candidates, so 'chosen' is never written by Pass 2
A cross-file match is written with evidence 'inferred' through promoteResolvedBatch, and a same-file one stays 'extracted' (the reader's)
Pass 2 never touches boundary kinds or rows awaiting an id; those stay with the endpoint passes and Pass 0
The entity index's existing maps (byId, byFile, fileEntities, byNameKindLang keyed by language family) are unchanged; CALLS/INHERITS/IMPLEMENTS resolution is unaffected
Settle mode still reads only the committed files' rows when no committed file defines a table or view

migration.stateBefore: The cross-file pass's Pass 2 resolves only CALLS, INHERITS and IMPLEMENTS (PASS2_KINDS, src/indexer/cross-file-resolver.ts:134; bundle c1). A pending SQL REFERENCES row to a table or view of another file is never attempted. A full index classes it 'no-candidate'/'not-attempted' (classifyUnattempted, src/indexer/cross-file-resolver.ts:262), and settle mode reads only the committed files' own rows (rowsInScope, src/indexer/cross-file-resolver.ts:503; bundle c3).
migration.stateAfter: Pass 2 also resolves a sql REFERENCES row by name among the repository's sql table/view entities: one candidate is promoted with evidence 'inferred', several are classed ambiguous, none is classed no-candidate/no-match. Settle mode also re-attempts the repository's pending sql REFERENCES rows whose name a committed file's table or view now matches.

migrationSteps.action: Add REFERENCES to the Pass 2 kinds, with a SQL name matcher and a SQL name index on the entity index
In settle mode, runPass2 also takes the pending sql REFERENCES rows whose name a committed file's table or view matches; rowsInScope and its other callers are unchanged

No data rewrite: rows already stored are re-attempted, and their classes updated, by the next full or repository pass, or by a settle that defines their name. Existing 'not-attempted' classes are replaced then.

migration.backwardCompat: Internal only: no request, field, kind, byte or schema version changes. An older daemon reading a store this one wrote sees ordinary REFERENCES edges, whose evidence byte is already known since s7. Rolling back leaves the promoted edges as valid edges.
